entities.summary:
The 2017 United Kingdom general election was a pivotal event in the country's electoral history, held on June 8, 2017. It was the third snap election called by Prime Minister Theresa May, who sought to gain a majority in the House of Commons for her Conservative Party. The election was significant because it marked a major shift in British politics, with the Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, gaining 30 seats and reducing the Conservative majority to just 17 seats.

The core events of the 2017 general election were the campaigns of the two main parties, the Conservative Party and the Labour Party. The Conservative Party campaigned on a platform of national security and stability, while the Labour Party focused on issues such as education, healthcare, and the economy. The election also saw the rise of the Liberal Democrats, who won 12 seats and became the third-largest party in the House of Commons.

The legacy of the 2017 general election was significant, as it marked a major shift in British politics and paved the way for the country's departure from the European Union. The election also saw the rise of young, diverse MPs, including many who had never held public office before. The election's impact can be seen in the UK's current politics, with many of the same issues and debates continuing to this day.

One lasting cultural footprint of the 2017 general election is the increased involvement of young people in politics, with many young people voting for the first time in their lives. This has had a lasting impact on British politics, with many young people continuing to be involved in politics and advocacy.
